intended_object: The interaction energy of a measure μ with interaction kernel W, i.e. (1/2)∫∫ W(x,y) dμ(x) dμ(y), taken as an extended real (+∞ when the positive part of W is not integrable). Source: the docstring, the module documentation and the references to McCann, Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré §9.3 and Santambrogio §7.3.
explanation:
The definition is `potentialEnergy (fun z ↦ W z / 2) (μ.prod μ)`. `potentialEnergy V ν` is ⊤ when ∫⁻ (V)⁺ dν = ∞. Otherwise it is ∫⁻ V⁺ − ∫⁻ V⁻ in EReal. This is the usual extended-real convention for ∫ V dν: +∞ when the positive part diverges, and possibly −∞ when only the negative part diverges. Here V = W/2 and ν = μ⊗μ, so the result is (1/2)∫∫ W d(μ⊗μ). The positive part of W/2 has infinite integral exactly when the positive part of W does, so the ⊤ case matches the docstring.

The 1/2 factor is the standard normalization in the Wasserstein gradient-flow literature (AGS, Santambrogio). A general kernel W(x,y) on X × X over an arbitrary measurable space includes the usual difference kernels w(x−y), so the definition is fully general.

Mathlib has no notion of interaction energy. The unused variable `Y` in the section is harmless.
